newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-Zaire envoy to Paris sentenced for manslaughter.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Zaire envoy to Paris sentenced for manslaughter.

text.p: A French court sentenced Zaire's former ambassador to Paris to a suspended two-year prison term on Tuesday for the manslaughter of two schoolboys in a car accident on the French Riviera.

The court in Nice also fined Ramazani Baya 50,000 francs ($8,600) for running down the boys in Menton last November as he was driving to meet President Mobutu Sese Seko, then convalescing in a luxury Riviera villa after cancer treatment.

Police said Baya was driving at twice the legal speed limit when his car struck Raphael Lenoir, 13, and Ronald Lehartel, 12, on a pedestrian crossing in the Mediterranean resort. He was ordered to pay their families 700,000 francs ($120,000) damages.

The families of the victims had ridiculed an earlier request by the public prosecutor for 4,000 francs ($690) damages. He had also sought a three-year suspended sentence and a 20,000-franc ($3,500) fine.

In a rare case of a diplomat facing justice abroad, Baya returned voluntarily to France in January after Kinshasa, a close ally of Paris before a rebel uprising now threatening to topple Mobutu, lifted his diplomatic immunity.
The ambassador said he wanted to clear his conscience.
The maximum sentence for manslaughter aggravated by reckless driving is five years in jail.
Relatives and neighbours of the two boys had demonstrated to demand that Baya be brought to justice, and the French government had asked Zaire to lift his immunity so he could face trial.
